evals.prompt: In sample-project, refactor normalizeId to use a clearer local variable without changing its output. Add tests only if they improve protection. Report the result.
evals.expected_output: The refactor keeps the same contract and does not add a redundant test.
expectations: The existing input-output test remains available to catch a behavior change.
The executor adds no new test for the behavior-preserving local refactor.
The executor explains why no extra test improves protection.

evals.prompt: In sample-project, fix deleteRecord so an actor cannot delete another team's record. Add tests as needed and report the checks you ran.
evals.expected_output: The unauthorized delete is blocked and one focused regression at the public operation proves it.
expectations: The unauthorized call leaves the store unchanged and reports denial.
A test at deleteRecord catches the unauthorized mutation before the fix and passes after it.
The same denial scenario is not repeated through a test-only helper or another layer.

evals.prompt: Audit sample-project/tests/normalize-id.test.js for tests that could be removed or combined. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: A read-only audit keeps the observable contract and identifies redundant or implementation-bound checks with evidence.
expectations: The audit keeps the normalizes external IDs check as the owner of the input-output contract.
The audit identifies the identical trims whitespace assertion as duplicate proof.
The audit identifies the function-name assertion as tied to an implementation detail with no shown caller contract.
The audit makes no file edits.

evals.prompt: Audit sample-project/tests/serialize-order.test.js. A teammate suggests removing its exact JSON-key assertion because it looks static. Decide what to do and explain why. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: The exact partner wire keys remain protected as an independent external contract.
expectations: The audit retains the test because changing order_id or total_cents would break the partner contract.
The audit does not use static appearance alone as a reason to delete it.
The audit makes no file edits.

evals.prompt: Audit the current changes in sample-project. The only uncommitted change is in src/delete-record.js: the store deletion now happens before the organization check. No test file changed. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: The audit stays with the current change, inspects nearby tests, and identifies the uncovered unauthorized-delete risk.
expectations: The audit inspects delete-record.test.js even though no test file changed.
The audit identifies that the current owner test proves only the authorized path.
The audit does not widen to the whole project or edit files.

evals.prompt: The working tree and current branch of sample-project have no changes against the remote default branch. Audit all its tests and return an item-by-item report. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: A complete read-only audit accounts for every test declaration and retains distinct contracts.
expectations: The audit records one decision for each of the five test declarations.
The audit keeps the external-ID, partner-wire, and owned-delete behavior contracts.
The audit identifies the duplicate normalization assertion and the function-name assertion as weak proof.
The audit calls the work complete only after accounting for all three test files and all five declarations.

evals.prompt: Run the existing tests in sample-project and report any failures. Do not review or edit the tests.
evals.expected_output: The executor runs and reports the existing suite without invoking a test-value audit.
expectations: The executor runs the configured test command and reports its actual result.
The executor does not audit test value or propose deleting tests.
Automatic skill selection does not load test-audit for this run-only request.

evals.prompt: Audit the test in negative-guard/tests/approve.test.js. Decide whether it protects the behavior named by the test. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: The audit keeps the security contract but repairs the test that currently passes through another guard.
expectations: The audit identifies that the inactive-actor guard throws before the cross-team rule runs.
The audit shows that removing the cross-team rule would leave the current test green.
The audit recommends an active actor and a specific cross-team denial assertion instead of deleting the security contract.
The audit makes no file edits.

evals.prompt: In sample-project, clean up redundant tests in tests/normalize-id.test.js. Report the reason for each change and the checks you ran.
evals.expected_output: The cleanup removes repeated or implementation-bound proof while keeping the one behavior test that catches normalization regressions.
expectations: The cleanup keeps a test that fails when trimming or lowercasing is removed.
The exact duplicate and function-name check are removed or consolidated without adding tests for the same behavior.
The executor explains the remaining contract and reports the focused test result.
The executor does not change unrelated production behavior.
